title: Tanzanian Beef Bone Soup
community: A nourishing everyday soup enjoyed across Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Supu ya Mifupa — Tanzanian bone broth soup. Large beef or goat bones slow-simmered for 2 hours with vegetables, ginger, and spices into a rich, deeply nourishing, golden broth. Tanzania's most restorative food — given to the sick, nursing mothers, and anyone who needs strength.
longDesc: Supu ya Mifupa is Tanzania's healing food — the soup given to the sick, the recovering, and new mothers. The 2-hour simmer extracts collagen, marrow, and minerals from the bones into a broth of extraordinary nutritional depth. Sold at roadside stalls in large pots, it is the working person's nourishment.
ingredients: 1 kg beef or goat bones — with marrow
steps: Blanch bones in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Place bones in a large pot with all vegetables, garlic, ginger, salt, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil. Skim foam.
Reduce to the lowest simmer. Cover and cook for 2 hours.
Serve garnished with coriander and a wedge of lemon.
chefTips: Blanching first removes blood and impurities — clearer broth.
The lowest possible simmer produces the clearest, most elegant broth.
Lemon squeezed at the table brightens the whole bowl.
cookingScience: Long simmering dissolves collagen from bones and connective tissue into gelatin — producing a broth that sets to a jelly when chilled. This gelatin is what makes bone broth uniquely nourishing and soothing to the digestive system.
sustainabilityTips: Bones would otherwise be discarded — supu ya mifupa uses every part of the animal.
culturalNote: Supu ya Mifupa is Tanzania's most healing food — given with love to the sick and the recovering. Every Tanzanian knows that a bowl of bone soup can restore strength when nothing else can.
